n: Lichen sclerosus of the vulva, biopsy
wrong: Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva

ww.Lichen simplex chronicus: Lichen simplex chronicus thickens the epidermis: scratching causes acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and long rete ridges with no atypia. This biopsy shows the opposite, a thin epidermis lying over pale, homogenized dermal collagen.
ww.Lichen planus: Lichen planus has a dense band of lymphocytes hugging the dermoepidermal junction and a saw-toothed epidermis. Here the pale collagen band sits directly under the epidermis and the lymphocytes lie deeper, below it.
ww.Differentiated vulvar intraepithelial ne: Differentiated VIN usually has a thickened epidermis with elongated rete ridges and atypical basal cells that mature early. This epidermis is thin and bland, and the main change is the pale dermal collagen.
ww.Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva: Extramammary Paget disease scatters large, pale, mucin-containing tumor cells singly and in nests through the epidermis. This epidermis is a thin ribbon of bland squamous cells with no such cells.

look: Read the layers from the top down. The epidermis is only a thin, flat ribbon, with no rete ridges, and beneath it lies a broad band of pale, homogenized pink collagen that has lost its fiber pattern and most of its cells. Deeper, a band of small dark lymphocytes marks the inflammation. A thin epidermis over a pale collagen band is lichen sclerosus.

findings: Thin epidermis: a narrow, flattened ribbon of squamous cells runs across the top with loss of the rete ridges, which explains the thin, wrinkled, parchment-like white skin seen in the clinic.

Homogenized dermal collagen: directly beneath the epidermis, a broad, pale pink band of collagen has lost its fiber pattern and almost all of its cells; this sclerosis gives the white color and later scarring.
Lymphocytic band: below the pale zone, a band of small dark lymphocytes lies in the deeper dermis, the T-cell mediated inflammation that causes the itching and drives the scarring.
